title: fix(components): a collapsible form section header is keyboard-operable (objectui#13220)
body:
Fixes #13220
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`SectionDivider` in `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` draws a form section header inline in a sectioned form (the record Create/Edit dialog, the drawer form, and the other `@object-ui/plugin-form` layouts that emit `section-divider` rows). A collapsible header was a `div` with `role="button"` and `aria-expanded` and only an `onClick`: no tab stop, no key handler. The Tab cycle stepped over it and a group that starts collapsed could only be opened with a mouse.

The collapsible header now also carries:

- `tabIndex={0}`, so it is in the Tab order, in document order between the field above it and the first field below the group;
- an `onKeyDown` that toggles on Enter and on Space. It calls `preventDefault` for both keys, so Space does not scroll the dialog. A keydown with `repeat` set (a held key) does not toggle again;
- the Shadcn Button's focus-ring classes (`ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2`), so keyboard focus is visible.

A header that is not collapsible is unchanged: no role, no tab stop, no `aria-expanded`. No export, prop or schema key is added. Nothing under `packages/components/src/ui/**` is touched. The record detail page's header is not touched.

## Why this route, and not a native button element

The dispatch suggested turning the header into a native button element with `type="button"`, as the record detail page's header became in objectui#12625. I measured that route first. These readers depend on the header's current DOM shape, and every one of them is a test file in `@object-ui/plugin-form`, outside this card's file surface:

- `[role="button"][aria-expanded]` is the selector that finds the control in `collapseResolution-9849`, `collapsedImpliesCollapsible-9780`, `headinglessCollapseDiagnostic-9849`, `modalSectionToggleSuspense-12559` and `objectFormSectionMembers-8071`. A native button has the button role only implicitly, so the attribute selector would find nothing.
- `.border-b span` (the headings) and `.border-b p` (the blurbs) are read as lists in `collapseResolution-9849`, `collapsedImpliesCollapsible-9780` and `objectFormSectionMembers-8071`. Inside a button the label line and the blurb would have to be phrasing content, which adds spans and drops the `p`. The blurb-only collapsible row (objectFormSectionMembers-8071 row 8) asserts zero heading spans and one blurb `p`.
- `ungroupedFieldSection-11777` clicks the row container itself, `closest('div.col-span-full')`. With the button inside the row, that click would no longer toggle the group.

The claim says to stop on a breach of the file surface, so I took the route that changes none of those readers. Both routes meet the card's acceptance: the header is reachable by Tab, Enter and Space toggle it, and it keeps `aria-expanded`. The native-button route is still open as a follow-up if the seat wants it. The reader list above is what that follow-up would edit.

There is no `aria-controls`. The group's fields are siblings of the header in the form's field grid, with no container element of their own, and a collapsed group's fields are not mounted at all (the containers hand them over `hidden`). The record detail page can point at its content because that content is a container. `aria-controls` is optional in the disclosure pattern.

## Mechanism assumptions, as measured

1. **Confirmed.** On unfixed `main` (`ab4e4d7`), the new test's Tab cycle stopped on the `code` input, the `note` input and the Create button. It never stopped on the collapsed "Money" header (4 of the 5 rows that existed then were red; listed under Tests).
2. **Read.** The detail page's header (`DetailSection`, objectui#12625) is a native button inside the card header, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` from Radix `CollapsibleTrigger`. The form header now behaves the same way for a keyboard: it is a Tab stop, Enter and Space toggle it, and its state is announced. Its element differs, for the reason above.
3. **Disproved as stated, then redirected.** The comment near the accessible-name code ("a `div[role="button"]`, just takes the name") is about the `file` widget's control, not about `SectionDivider`. The real readers of the header's shape are the plugin-form tests listed above. All of them stay correct because this change only adds attributes and classes.

## Tests

New: `packages/components/src/renderers/form/__tests__/form-section-header-keyboard-13220.test.tsx`. The test harness keeps the collapse state the way `ModalForm` does: the header row carries `collapsible`, `collapsed` and `onToggle`, and a collapsed member is handed over `hidden`. Rows:

- Tab reaches the collapsed header, between the field above it and the field below the group.
- A plain heading is not a Tab stop and carries no role, `tabindex` or `aria-expanded`. This is read off the same Tab cycle that does stop on the collapsible header.
- Enter opens the group, focus stays on the header, and the next Tab lands on its first field. Shift+Tab and Enter close it again. The form is not submitted.
- Space opens and closes the group. The form is not submitted.
- Space's default is prevented. A `repeat` keydown of Space, and then one of Enter, does not toggle (one key per reading, so two toggles cannot cancel out). Any other key is neither prevented nor a toggle.
- Control: Enter in a field still submits the form, so the no-submit assertions can fail.

Runs (repo root, through the shared verify lock):

- Unfixed `main` + new test: `Tests  4 failed | 1 passed (5)`. Example: `AssertionError: expected [ input …(7), …(2) ] to include div …(3)`, meaning the Tab stops never included the header. The 4 failures were the Tab, plain-heading, Enter and Space rows. The control row passed.
- Fix, head `cc91445`: `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  6 passed (6)`.
- Ablations on head `cc91445`, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor hit exactly once, the change was verified on disk, then restored with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`):
  - drop `tabIndex`: `Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)`
  - drop the `repeat` guard: `Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)`, `expected 'false' to be 'true'`
  - drop `preventDefault`: `Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)`, `expected true to be false`
- Readers and consumers, head `cc91445`: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/components/src/renderers/form/ packages/plugin-form/ apps/console/src/components/FormPage.sectionGroup.test.tsx` gave `Test Files  274 passed (274)`, `Tests  2912 passed | 18 skipped (2930)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

## Local gates (head `cc91445`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (after `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/components^...' --concurrency=2`): exit 0. The script echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. `--listFilesOnly` on the test project lists the new test file once.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. It reports 2 source files of 1 released package changed and 1 changeset declared.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, `0 new citation(s)`.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.

The repo-wide lint and the full test farm are CI's.

## Browser reading

Not run here. Where to see it: the showcase object `showcase_semantic_zoo` has a field group `money` with `collapse: 'collapsed'`. Open that object's Create dialog in the console and press Tab from the Code field. Focus should land on the "Money" header, and Enter or Space should open the group. Header selector: `form div.col-span-full[role="button"][aria-expanded]` with text "Money".

## Acceptance notes

- Changeset: `.changeset/13220-section-header-keyboard.md`, `@object-ui/components` `patch`.
- If the native-button form is wanted later, its cost is the reader edits listed above. It would also put the blurb outside the button, so the accessible name would become the label alone, as on the detail page. Today the name is the label plus the blurb, because a `div` with `role="button"` takes its name from all of its content. That is unchanged by this PR.
